name: Tangerine
tagline: A native Mac app for tracking daily habits and routines, sold direct from its own site.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is trivial: a list of habits, a set of dates, a streak count. An agent can produce a working SwiftUI menu bar tracker with local storage in one sitting, and it will do the thing. What it will not produce is the part people actually buy a native Mac app for: the animations, the keyboard handling, the widgets, the iOS counterpart that syncs over iCloud so you can tick a box from bed. Habit apps also live or die on whether you keep opening them, and a build you made yourself tends to lose that fight around day nine. Buildable, genuinely, with the polish gap sitting exactly where the product is.
coreLoopDIY: A local SwiftUI menu bar app where you define habits, tick them off each day, and see a streak grid, with everything stored in a JSON file on disk.
requirements: willingness to ship an unsigned local build or pay for a developer certificate
whatYouLose: An iPhone app and iCloud sync, which is where most habit ticking actually happens
Widgets, notifications and Shortcuts support that feel native rather than bolted on
Visual polish: the grid, the animations, the small satisfactions that make you come back
Someone else maintaining it across macOS releases
Any reminder system you did not remember to build
moatNotes: The moat is taste and native plumbing, not technology. Nothing stops you, the output just looks like a weekend project because it is one.
whyPeopleStillPay: A habit tracker is a behavioural product wearing a software costume. The code is a checkbox and a date array; the value is that opening it feels good enough that you do it 200 days in a row, which comes from motion design, a phone app in your pocket, and sync that never loses a tick. Paying once for a native Mac app that someone else keeps alive through OS updates is a rounding error against the cost of abandoning your own version in week two.
notes: The logic is a weekend; the reason you keep using it is not.
prompt:
Build a native macOS habit tracker called Streaks Local. Single Xcode project, no server, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack: Swift 5.9+, SwiftUI, targeting macOS 14+. Use SwiftData for persistence with the store in Application Support. No third party packages.

App shape:
- A menu bar extra (MenuBarExtra) with a tangerine-ish SF Symbol, showing today's completion count as the label.
- Clicking it opens a popover listing today's habits as tappable rows with a checkbox, name, and current streak.
- A separate main window, opened from the popover, with: habit management (add, rename, archive, reorder, set an emoji and a colour) and a year grid view per habit showing filled cells for completed days.

Data model:
- Habit: id, name, emoji, colorHex, cadence (daily, or N times per week), createdAt, archivedAt.
- Completion: habitId, date (day granularity, stored as a local-calendar day key), createdAt.
- Streak logic computed, not stored. Respect cadence: a weekly-target habit does not break its streak on an off day.

Must have:
- Keyboard driven: arrow keys to move between today's habits, space to toggle, cmd+comma for settings.
- Local notifications via UserNotifications for an optional daily reminder time. Ask permission only when the user enables it.
- Export and import all data as JSON from the settings screen, so the data is never trapped.
- Launch at login toggle using SMAppService.

Explicitly out of scope: iOS app, iCloud sync, widgets, charts beyond the year grid, social features, any paid API.

Ship a README with build instructions and a note that the build is unsigned unless the user supplies their own developer certificate. Put nothing secret in the repo; there are no secrets in this app.
